## 🎓 Today's lesson
**What is a Variable Rate Repo (VRR) Auction?**
When commercial banks in India face sudden cash shortages or need liquidity to fund massive events like public stock offerings, they borrow overnight from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Instead of lending at a fixed repo rate, the RBI uses a **Variable Rate Repo (VRR) auction**—like the ₹50,000 crore auction held today—where banks bid against each other by offering different interest rates they are willing to pay [[RBI (official)]](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63843). The highest interest rate bids win the funds until the cut-off point is reached (today's weighted average rate landed at 5.55%). This allows the central bank to control short-term money supply dynamically based on actual market demand.
